back: The statistical study of human populations including size, structure, and distribution

front: What is the current world population (approximate)?
back: About 8 billion people (as of 2024)
The average number of children born to a woman over her lifetime

front: What replacement-level fertility rate is needed to maintain population?
back: Approximately 2.1 children per woman

front: What is the demographic transition model?
back: A model showing how populations shift from high birth/death rates to low birth/death rates as countries develop
The average number of years a person is expected to live based on current mortality rates

front: Which continent has the highest population growth rate?
back: Africa
The ratio of non-working age population (young and old) to working-age population
The increasing proportion of a population living in urban areas

front: What percentage of the world population lives in urban areas?
back: Over 55% (and increasing)
A graphical representation showing the age and sex distribution of a population
The difference between immigration (in) and emigration (out) of an area

front: What is the median age of the world population?
back: About 30 years

front: Which country has the oldest median age?
back: Monaco (approximately 55 years)

front: Which country has the youngest median age?
back: Niger (approximately 15 years)

front: What is the infant mortality rate?
back: The number of deaths of infants under one year per 1,000 live births
An official count of a population typically including demographic information

front: What is the crude birth rate?
back: The number of live births per 1,000 people per year

front: What is the crude death rate?
back: The number of deaths per 1,000 people per year
The birth rate minus the death rate (excluding migration)

front: What is the most spoken native language?
back: Mandarin Chinese (about 920 million native speakers)

front: What is the most spoken language overall (including second language speakers)?
back: English (approximately 1.5 billion speakers)
The number of people per unit of area (usually per km² or per square mile)
Economic growth potential from changes in age structure when working-age population exceeds dependents
A population with an increasing proportion of elderly people
The ratio of males to females in a population
Movement of people within a country's borders
Emigration of highly skilled or educated individuals from a country
The maximum population size an environment can sustain indefinitely
